items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: But they had a piano player who was named Eddie Miller, that made music rolls for player piano; he'd go to Chicago and make music rolls for player piano, QRS and whatever they called them... And we jammed with these guys.

ctx.x: Let me just get back to the factual side of things. Chronologically almost, we've got you to the point whereby you said you went to St. Louis. You left the medicine show in St. Louis?

No. Not at first. When I got through in St. Louis, we went up, played up through Illinois and parts of Ohio. And we wound up in Harrisburg, Illinois. We was playing in Harrisburg, which at that time was called Bloody Williamson County, where they had bunches of syndicate... They had a bunch of roadhouses in those days and bootlegging joints.
